### 6:00 PM, a case from one trace

Stage 2, fourth item. Until now a case file was written by hand: someone had to know the failing input, what it should have produced, and both ends of the range. `whodunit open-case --from-trace <id>` writes the file from one failing run and stops.

- It looks for the run in neatroots, and in neatlogs cloud if neatroots does not have it.
- The input is the root span's. The bad ref is the commit in the run_info tags.
- The expected result is what the nearest earlier run of the same input paid, among runs that passed. A run passed if it was not flagged and paid something different from the failing run.
- The good ref comes from `whodunit/onset.py`: every run of that input, judged against the expected result, goes through the same change-point model the lineup uses, and the range starts where that model is 99% sure nothing had gone wrong yet.
- If no earlier run passed, it asks one question: what should this request have produced? Away from a keyboard it prints the question, writes nothing and exits, and `--expect` gives the answer.
- A trace does not say how to build and run the agent, so that is copied from another case for the same agent.

Tried on the real traces, on an ordinary run from the traffic that refunded 30.00 on someone else's order. From the trace id alone it wrote a case with the right request, an expected result of no refund taken from a run 11 hours of traffic earlier, and a range of 41 suspects that holds the real culprit. That file went to a scratch folder and is not in `cases/`.

What it cannot do: the earlier runs of the same input are read from neatroots only. A trace that exists only in the cloud gets its input and its bad ref, and then has to be told the expected result and the good ref. And "passed" leans on neatroots' own flags, so a run that was wrong without being flagged, and wrong in a different way from the failing one, could be taken for the expected result. The file's first lines name the run the expectation came from, so a person can check it.

### 6:21 PM, when no commit did it
# Sealed eval, 11 October 2026

Five regressions were planted in the refund agent's history by a second coding session, through ordinary requests to fresh coding sessions. It wrote the answer key, and the key's SHA-256 was committed in 4c45f7f before Whodunit ran on any case. `eval/score.py` checks the key against that hash before scoring. The key was added to git only after every case had been run.

Replays ran on the hackathon gateway's small model, three at a time.

## Result

With 120 replays allowed per case: 3 of 5 solved, 0 wrong accusations, 2 cases where nobody was named.

The two open cases were then resumed from their own replays with up to 200 more allowed: 5 of 5 solved, 0 wrong accusations.

| Case | Rate the second session measured | Rate Whodunit estimated | At 120 replays | In the end | Replays | Commits replayed | Suspects |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| cents-off | 100% | 93% | solved | solved | 21 | 5 | 13 |
| wrong-order-refunded | 30% | 12% | nobody named | solved | 168 | 9 | 12 |
| half-done-batch | 25% | 14% | nobody named | solved | 168 | 10 | 15 |
| strangers-paid | 72% | 59% | solved | solved | 30 | 5 | 11 |
| turned-away | 100% | 93% | solved | solved | 24 | 6 | 14 |

The rate Whodunit estimates is a posterior mean, so after only a few replays it sits below 100% even for a bug that fails every time.

## What it cost

Replay spend on the gateway, estimated from token counts at list prices, came to about $1.91 for all five cases:

- cents-off: about $0.08 (61,267 tokens)
- wrong-order-refunded: about $0.57 (438,034 tokens)
- half-done-batch: about $1.04 (795,110 tokens)
- strangers-paid: about $0.10 (78,530 tokens)
- turned-away: about $0.12 (100,111 tokens)

## What this does and does not show

- No commit was wrongly accused, at either budget. Five cases cannot show how often that would hold. The simulator puts a number on it for cases shaped like the two rare ones: with 320 replays allowed, about 4% of accusations name the wrong commit, and with 120 about 13%. See `eval/simulator/README.md`. On `half-done-batch` the top suspect at 120 replays was the wrong commit, at 53%, and Whodunit named nobody. That is the behaviour the 95% bar is for.
- The two cases it could not close at 120 replays are the two that fail least often. Whodunit put them at 12% and 14%, where the second session had measured 30% and 25% from a handful of probes. A bug that rare needs a lot of replays whatever the method.
- The ranges are short, 11 to 15 suspects. On ranges this size a careful scan from the oldest commit would have replayed about as many commits as Whodunit did, so this eval says little about savings on long histories. The simulator in `eval/simulator` covers 40 suspects.
- Five cases is a small sample. It is enough to say the pipeline works on a history it did not write, and not enough to put a number on accuracy.
- Each case has one planted regression inside its range, by design. Two regressions that touch the same inputs in one range are outside what the model assumes.

## What happened after the culprits were named

The owner's ruling was patch for all three kinds of change involved. A fix is kept when its failure rate is 95% likely to be back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit. The last column gives what the replays of the kept fix showed and the 95% upper bound on its failure rate. Clearing the bar is not proof: in simulation a fix that still fails 4 runs in 100 clears it about one time in three.

| Case | Outcome | Tries | Replays of the final fix, and the most it could still fail at 95% |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| cents-off | patch kept | 1 | 0 failures in 30, at most 6.2% |
| strangers-paid | patch kept | 1 | 0 failures in 30, at most 6.2% |
| wrong-order-refunded | patch kept | 1 | 0 failures in 36, at most 5.2% |
| turned-away | two patches fell short, then a revert was kept | 3 | 0 failures in 30, at most 6.2% |
| half-done-batch | not fixed | 3 | two patches left 5 failures in 90 each, at most 10.6%, and the revert conflicts |

So four of five were closed, one of them only by giving up on the patch the owner asked for, and one was left open and says so.

## The same culprit across the whole history

`cases/whole-history.toml` takes the `strangers-paid` regression and widens the range to the whole grown history, 57 suspects. With alibis from entire-graph for 22 of them and 18 ordinary runs as evidence, 20 replays across 5 commits named the culprit at 99.8%. A scan from the oldest suspect would have tested 37 commits. This is the run that speaks to savings on a longer history, and it is one run. Run again with no alibis and no ordinary runs to go on, it took 30 replays across 8 commits to reach 95.4%. So the head start saved 10 replays and 3 commits, in one run each way, with the two kinds of help taken away together.

Both runs were made again on Monday 12 October, from nothing. With the head start: 20 replays across 5 commits, 98.3%. Without it: 33 replays across 8 commits, 99.0%. That run also went on to the fix, and its first patch was rejected by the do-no-harm check. `cases/whole-history.casefile.html` has it.

=== agent/__main__.py
import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from typing import Any

from agent.loop import run_agent
from agent.provider import get_provider
from agent.tracing import CASE_SPAN, init_tracing, shutdown_tracing, span


def format_tool_calls(tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    """Human-readable listing of each tool call's name, args and result."""
    if not tool_calls:
        return "Tool calls: none"
    lines = [f"Tool calls ({len(tool_calls)}):"]
    for i, tc in enumerate(tool_calls, 1):
        args = ", ".join(f"{k}={json.dumps(v)}" for k, v in tc["args"].items())
        lines.append(f"  {i}. {tc['name']}({args})")
        result = json.dumps(tc["result"], indent=2).replace("\n", "\n       ")
        lines.append(f"     -> {result}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m agent")
    parser.add_argument("message", help="customer message")
    parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true",
                        help="also print each tool call and its result (to stderr) after the reply")
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    except SystemExit as e:
        return int(e.code or 0)
    init_tracing()  # before the client is created so it can be wrapped
    try:
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        with span(CASE_SPAN, "WORKFLOW"):
            result = run_agent(args.message, get_provider())
        latency_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000, 1)  # total wall-clock: model calls + tools
        print(json.dumps({**result.to_dict(), "latency_ms": latency_ms}, indent=2), flush=True)
        if args.verbose:
            # stderr so stdout stays parseable JSON
            print(format_tool_calls(result.tool_calls), file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
    finally:
        shutdown_tracing()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
=== agent/provider.py
"""Model provider layer.

A Provider turns (system, messages, tools) into a normalized Response. Select with env AGENT_PROVIDER
("anthropic" is the default; "scripted" is for tests and is constructed directly).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol

DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"  # the support agent is PINNED to Haiku tier; see evals/models.py


@dataclass
class Response:
    """Normalized model response. `content` is a list of Anthropic-style blocks:
    {"type": "text", "text": ...} or {"type": "tool_use", "id": ..., "name": ..., "input": {...}}."""

    content: list[dict[str, Any]]
    stop_reason: str = "end_turn"
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return "".join(b["text"] for b in self.content if b["type"] == "text")

    @property
    def tool_uses(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        return [b for b in self.content if b["type"] == "tool_use"]


class Provider(Protocol):
    def create(self, *, system: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], tools: list[dict[str, Any]],
               max_tokens: int = 1024) -> Response: ...


class AnthropicProvider:
    """Anthropic Messages API. Key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, model from AGENT_MODEL, temperature 0."""

    def __init__(self, client: Any | None = None, model: str | None = None) -> None:
        if client is None:
            from anthropic import Anthropic

            from agent.tracing import wrap_client

            client = wrap_client(Anthropic())  # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
        self.client = client
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("AGENT_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL)

    def create(self, *, system, messages, tools, max_tokens=1024) -> Response:
        r = self.client.messages.create(
            model=self.model, max_tokens=max_tokens,
            extra_body={"temperature": 0},  # SDK 1.x dropped the typed kwarg; the API still accepts it
            system=system, messages=messages, tools=tools,
        )
        blocks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for b in r.content:
            if b.type == "text":
                blocks.append({"type": "text", "text": b.text})
            elif b.type == "tool_use":
                blocks.append({"type": "tool_use", "id": b.id, "name": b.name, "input": dict(b.input)})
        return Response(blocks, r.stop_reason or "end_turn", r.usage.input_tokens, r.usage.output_tokens)


@dataclass
class ScriptedProvider:
    """Replays a fixed list of Responses (for tests). Records every call in `calls`."""

    script: list[Response]
    calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)

    def create(self, *, system, messages, tools, max_tokens=1024) -> Response:
        self.calls.append({"system": system, "messages": [dict(m) for m in messages], "tools": tools})
        if not self.script:
            raise RuntimeError("ScriptedProvider script exhausted")
        return self.script.pop(0)


# EXTENSION POINT: add other backends (AWS Bedrock, `claude` CLI, ...) as classes implementing
# Provider.create and register them in _FACTORIES. Not implemented on purpose.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from agent.logs import log_message_truncated, log_tool_call
from agent.prompt import SYSTEM_PROMPT
from agent.provider import Provider
from agent.tracing import current_trace_id, set_json, span, traced
from tools import ToolBox

MAX_STEPS = 12  # model calls per run; leaves room for verification searches and retries
MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS = 2000  # longer customer messages are truncated (and the truncation logged)
_UNKNOWN_ORDER = re.compile(r"^order '(.*)' not found$")


def unknown_order_reply(order_id: str) -> str:
    return (f"Sorry, I couldn't find an order with the number {order_id}. Could you double-check the order "
            "number and send it again? Is there anything else we can help with?")


def _guard_unknown_order(reply: str, tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    """Replace a reply that echoes a raw 'order ... not found' tool error with a customer-friendly apology."""
    for tc in tool_calls:
        err = tc["result"].get("error", "")
        m = _UNKNOWN_ORDER.match(err)
        if m and err.lower() in reply.lower():
            return unknown_order_reply(m.group(1))
    return reply


@dataclass
class RunResult:
    reply: str
    tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)  # {name, args, result}
    steps: int = 0
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    trace_id: str = ""
    hit_step_limit: bool = False

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)


def run_agent(message: str, provider: Provider, toolbox: ToolBox | None = None,
              max_steps: int | None = None) -> RunResult:
    """Run one customer message through the agent. `max_steps` defaults to MAX_STEPS.
    Messages longer than MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS are truncated to that length."""
    if len(message) > MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS:
        log_message_truncated(len(message), MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS)
        message = message[:MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS]
    return _run(message, provider, toolbox or ToolBox(), max_steps or MAX_STEPS)


@traced
def _run(message: str, provider: Provider, toolbox: ToolBox, max_steps: int) -> RunResult:
    res = RunResult(reply="", trace_id=current_trace_id())
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "user", "content": message}]
    for _ in range(max_steps):
        r = provider.create(system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, messages=messages, tools=toolbox.schemas)
        res.steps += 1
        res.input_tokens += r.input_tokens
        res.output_tokens += r.output_tokens
        if not r.tool_uses:
            res.reply = _guard_unknown_order(r.text, res.tool_calls)
            return res
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": r.content})
        results = []
        for tu in r.tool_uses:
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            with span(f"tool:{tu['name']}", "TOOL", **{"tool.name": tu["name"]}) as sp:
                set_json(sp, "tool.args", tu["input"])
                out = toolbox.call(tu["name"], tu["input"])
                set_json(sp, "tool.result", out)
                if isinstance(out, dict) and "error" in out:
                    sp.set_attribute("tool.error", str(out["error"])[:500])
            log_tool_call(tu["name"], tu["input"], (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
            res.tool_calls.append({"name": tu["name"], "args": tu["input"], "result": out})
            results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": tu["id"], "content": json.dumps(out)})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
        res.reply = r.text
    res.hit_step_limit = True
    if not res.reply:
        res.reply = "Sorry, I could not finish handling this request. A human agent will follow up."
    return res

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import contextvars
import json
import os
import uuid
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator

WORKFLOW_NAME = "support-agent"
CASE_SPAN = "support_case"  # name of the per-case parent span opened by the harness / CLI
_enabled = False
_trace_id: contextvars.ContextVar[str] = contextvars.ContextVar("trace_id", default="")


def run_tags() -> list[str]:
    """Tags from env: AGENTBISECT_COMMIT, AGENTBISECT_RUN_ID, AGENTBISECT_CASE."""
    out = []
    for env, key in (("AGENTBISECT_COMMIT", "commit"), ("AGENTBISECT_RUN_ID", "run"), ("AGENTBISECT_CASE", "case")):
        if os.environ.get(env):
            out.append(f"{key}:{os.environ[env]}")
    return out


def init_tracing() -> bool:
    """Call once per process, before creating the model client. Tags are process-wide in neatlogs."""
    global _enabled
    if _enabled:
        return True
    if not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"):
        return False
    try:
        import neatlogs

        neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], workflow_name=WORKFLOW_NAME, tags=run_tags())
        _enabled = True
    except Exception:  # tracing must never break the agent
        _enabled = False
    return _enabled


def wrap_client(client: Any) -> Any:
    if not _enabled:
        return client
    import neatlogs

    return neatlogs.wrap(client)

import json

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CaseInput:
    text: str
    expect: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # what the check compares against, e.g. {"refunds": [...]}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Case:
    id: str
    symptom: str
    good: str
    bad: str
    inputs: tuple[CaseInput, ...]
    target: str = "."  # folder inside the repo that holds the agent
    build: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # run once per worktree; a failure skips the commit
    run: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # "{input}" is replaced with the input text
    check: dict = field(default_factory=lambda: {"kind": "refunds"})
    env: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    timeout: float = 120.0
    fixed: str = ""  # the commit that fixed it, once the case is closed and kept as a regression test
    traffic_sent_by: str = ""  # who sent the agent's ordinary runs, when it was a script and not real users
    # How the agent says "the model provider or the network failed, and my own code did not". A replay
    # that ends this way is voided and run again, and is never evidence about the commit.
    void_exit_codes: tuple[int, ...] = ()  # exit codes the agent keeps for that
    void_stderr: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # for commits from before it had one: text on the last line of stderr, with a non-zero exit

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> "Case":
        data = tomllib.loads(Path(path).read_text())
        inputs = tuple(
            CaseInput(text=i["text"], expect={k: v for k, v in i.items() if k != "text"}) for i in data.pop("inputs")
        )
        for key in ("build", "run", "void_exit_codes", "void_stderr"):
            data[key] = tuple(data.get(key, ()))
        return cls(inputs=inputs, **data)


def last_json_line(stdout: str) -> dict | None:
    """The agent prints its result as one JSON object on the last line that parses."""
    for line in reversed(stdout.strip().splitlines()):
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith("{"):
            try:
                return json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
    return None


def _same_refunds(got: list[dict], want: list[dict]) -> bool:
    def key(r):
        return (str(r.get("order_id")), float(r.get("refunded", 0)))

    got, want = sorted(map(key, got)), sorted(map(key, want))
    return len(got) == len(want) and all(g[0] == w[0] and math.isclose(g[1], w[1], abs_tol=0.005) for g, w in zip(got, want))


def judge(case: Case, case_input: CaseInput, stdout: str, cwd: Path) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Return (passed, reason) for one run of the agent."""
    kind = case.check.get("kind", "refunds")
    result = last_json_line(stdout)
    if kind == "refunds":
        if result is None:
            return False, "the agent printed no JSON result"
        want = case_input.expect.get("refunds", [])
        got = result.get("refunds", [])
        if _same_refunds(got, want):
            return True, f"refunds match: {json.dumps(got)}"
        return False, f"refunds were {json.dumps(got)}, expected {json.dumps(want)}"
    if kind == "command":
        # The command gets the agent's stdout on stdin and the expectation in WHODUNIT_EXPECT. Exit 0 is a pass.
        done = subprocess.run(
            case.check["command"], input=stdout, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd, timeout=case.timeout,
            env={**os.environ, "WHODUNIT_EXPECT": json.dumps(case_input.expect)},
        )
        reason = (done.stdout.strip() or done.stderr.strip()).splitlines()[-1:] or [f"exit {done.returncode}"]
        return done.returncode == 0, reason[0]
    raise ValueError(f"check kind {kind!r} is not one of refunds, command")

"""Replay a case's inputs against a commit, in a git worktree of its own."""

import hashlib
import os
import signal
import subprocess
import threading
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from .case import Case, CaseInput, judge, last_json_line
from .neat import unnamed
from .suspects import git, resolve

PASS, FAIL, SKIP = "pass", "fail", "skip"
VOID = "void"  # the provider or the network failed every time it was tried, so the replay says nothing about the commit
VOID_WAITS = (2.0, 8.0)  # seconds to wait before the second and the third attempt after a provider error


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Replay:
    sha: str
    input: str
    verdict: str  # pass, fail, skip or void
    reason: str
    seconds: float
    started: float = 0.0  # wall clock, seconds since the epoch
    tag: str = ""  # the case tag this replay's run carries in its trace, unique to the replay
    voided: int = 0  # attempts that hit a provider or network error and were thrown away
    timeouts: int = 0  # attempts that ran out of time
    model: str = ""  # a fingerprint of the model id the agent reported, if it reported one. Not the id itself.
    lock: str = ""  # the first 12 characters of the hash of the lockfile it ran with


def run_command(command: list[str], cwd: Path, env: dict, timeout: float) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Like subprocess.run, but a timeout stops the whole process group.

    The replay command is usually `uv run ...`, which starts the agent as a child. Killing only
    `uv` would leave the agent running.
    """
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, start_new_session=True)
    try:
        stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        try:
            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            pass
        process.communicate()
        raise
    return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)


class Runner:
    """Keeps one worktree per commit under .whodunit/worktrees and counts every replay it runs."""

    def __init__(self, repo: str | Path, case: Case, keep: bool = False):
        self.repo = Path(repo).resolve()
        self.case = case
        self.keep = keep
        # One folder per runner, so two runs in the same repo never remove each other's worktrees.
        self.root = self.repo / ".whodunit" / "worktrees" / str(os.getpid())
        self.built: dict[str, str | None] = {}  # sha -> None if the build worked, else why it did not
        self.replays: list[Replay] = []
        self._locks: dict[str, threading.Lock] = defaultdict(threading.Lock)  # one build at a time per commit
        self._turn: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)  # which input a commit gets next
        self._count = 0
        self._first = int(time.time()) % 100000 * 1000  # so tags from separate runs of one case never collide
        self.void_waits: tuple[float, ...] = VOID_WAITS
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.repo), "worktree", "prune"], capture_output=True)

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        if not self.keep:
            self.clean()

    def worktree(self, sha: str) -> Path:
        path = self.root / sha[:12]
        if not path.exists():
            self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            git(self.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", "--force", str(path), sha)
        return path

    def clean(self) -> None:
        for sha in list(self.built):
            path = self.root / sha[:12]
            if path.exists():
                subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.repo), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path)], capture_output=True)
        self.built.clear()
        try:
            self.root.rmdir()
        except OSError:
            pass

    def _lock(self, sha: str) -> str:
        """The hash of the agent's lockfile at this commit, or nothing if it has none."""
        lock = self.root / sha[:12] / self.case.target / "uv.lock"
        return hashlib.sha256(lock.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12] if lock.is_file() else ""

    def _env(self, sha: str, tag: str = "") -> dict:
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "VIRTUAL_ENV"}
        env.update(self.case.env)
        env["WHODUNIT_COMMIT"] = sha
        if self.case.id:
            env["WHODUNIT_CASE"] = tag or self.case.id
        else:
            env.pop("WHODUNIT_CASE", None)  # ordinary traffic carries no case tag
        digest = self._lock(sha)
        if digest:
            # Worktrees with the same lockfile share one environment, so a new commit does not
            # mean a new install. A commit that changes the lockfile gets its own.
            env.setdefault("UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT", str(self.repo / ".whodunit" / "envs" / digest))
        dotenv = self.repo / ".env"
        if dotenv.is_file():
            env.setdefault("WHODUNIT_ENV", str(dotenv))  # a path only; the agent reads the keys itself
        return env

    def build(self, sha: str) -> str | None:
        """Check the commit out and build it once. Returns why it failed, or None."""
        with self._locks[sha]:
            return self._build(sha)

    def _build(self, sha: str) -> str | None:
        if sha in self.built:
            return self.built[sha]
        problem = None
        cwd = self.worktree(sha) / self.case.target
        if not cwd.is_dir():
            problem = f"{self.case.target} does not exist at this commit"
        elif self.case.build:
            try:
                done = run_command(list(self.case.build), cwd, self._env(sha), self.case.timeout)
                if done.returncode != 0:
                    problem = "build failed: " + ((done.stderr.strip() or done.stdout.strip()).splitlines() or ["no output"])[-1]
            except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
                problem = f"build failed: {exc}"
        self.built[sha] = problem
        return problem

    def _provider_failed(self, done: subprocess.CompletedProcess) -> str:
        """Why this run says nothing about the commit, if it ended in a provider or network error. Empty otherwise."""
        lines = [line.strip() for line in done.stderr.splitlines() if line.strip()] or [""]
        if done.returncode in self.case.void_exit_codes:
            said = next((line for line in reversed(lines) if "provider error" in line or any(text in line for text in self.case.void_stderr)), lines[-1])
            return unnamed(said) or f"exit {done.returncode}"
        # An agent from before it had an exit code for this dies on the exception, which is then the last thing it prints.
        if done.returncode != 0 and any(text in lines[-1] for text in self.case.void_stderr):
            return unnamed(lines[-1])
        return ""

    def replay(self, ref: str, case_input: CaseInput) -> Replay:
        """Run the agent once at this commit with this input and judge the result.

        Two kinds of run are not judged. One that ends in a provider or network error is voided
        and run again, up to three attempts, and if every attempt goes that way the verdict is
        void. One that runs out of time gets a single further try with double the limit. If
        that one finishes it is judged like any other, and if it runs out of time too the
        verdict is a failure, because a commit that hangs is a real bug.
        """
        sha = resolve(self.repo, ref)
        started, clock = time.monotonic(), time.time()
        with self._locks["#"]:
            self._count += 1
            # The agent writes WHODUNIT_CASE into its trace, so a number after the case id lets
            # one replay be matched to exactly one run afterwards.
            tag = f"{self.case.id}/{self._first + self._count}" if self.case.id else ""
        problem = self.build(sha)
        voided = timeouts = 0
        model = ""
        if problem:
            verdict, reason = SKIP, problem
        else:
            cwd = self.worktree(sha) / self.case.target
            command = [part.replace("{input}", case_input.text) for part in self.case.run]
            limit = self.case.timeout
            while True:
                try:
                    done = run_command(command, cwd, self._env(sha, tag), limit)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    timeouts += 1
                    if timeouts == 1:
                        limit *= 2
                        continue
                    verdict, reason = FAIL, f"timed out twice, after {self.case.timeout:.0f}s and then {limit:.0f}s"
                    break
                trouble = self._provider_failed(done)
                if trouble:
                    voided += 1
                    if voided <= len(self.void_waits):
                        time.sleep(self.void_waits[voided - 1])
                        continue
                    verdict, reason = VOID, f"the provider or the network failed on all {voided} attempts: {trouble}"
                    break
                passed, reason = judge(self.case, case_input, done.stdout, cwd)
                reported = (last_json_line(done.stdout) or {}).get("model")
                if reported:
                    # Which model answered matters when a range turns out to be clear. The record names no model, so it keeps a fingerprint.
                    model = hashlib.sha256(str(reported).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
                if not passed and done.returncode != 0:
                    reason = f"exit {done.returncode}: " + unnamed((done.stderr.strip().splitlines() or [reason])[-1])
                verdict = PASS if passed else FAIL
                break

"""The suspects: every commit after the last good ref, up to and including the first bad one."""

import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

# A commit that never touched the agent's folder can still be guilty (a shared file, a
# lockfile higher up), so it keeps a small prior. Plain bisect ignores priors.
PRIOR_TOUCHES_TARGET = 1.0
PRIOR_ELSEWHERE = 0.05


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Suspect:
    sha: str
    subject: str
    files: tuple[str, ...]
    checkpoint: str | None  # Entire checkpoint id from the commit trailer
    touches_target: bool
    prior: float
    alibi: str = ""  # why this commit starts with less suspicion, when entire-graph gives a reason

    @property
    def short(self) -> str:
        return self.sha[:12]


def git(repo: str | Path, *args: str) -> str:
    done = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if done.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed: {done.stderr.strip()}")
    return done.stdout


def resolve(repo: str | Path, ref: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{ref}^{{commit}}").strip()


def list_suspects(repo: str | Path, good: str, bad: str, target: str = ".", graph: bool = False) -> list[Suspect]:
    """Commits in good..bad, oldest first. The last one is the bad ref itself.

    The path filter gives the first prior: a commit that never touched the agent's folder keeps
    a small one. With `graph`, entire-graph refines it for the commits that did, by asking
    whether what they changed is something the agent runs.
    """
    shas = git(repo, "rev-list", "--reverse", "--ancestry-path", f"{good}..{bad}").split()
    prefix = "" if target in (".", "") else target.rstrip("/") + "/"
    suspects = []
    for sha in shas:
        subject, _, trailer = git(
            repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%s%x00%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly,separator=%x20)", sha
        ).strip().partition("\x00")
        files = tuple(git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-m", "--first-parent", sha).split("\n"))
        files = tuple(f for f in files if f)
        touches = any(f.startswith(prefix) for f in files)
        prior, alibi = (PRIOR_TOUCHES_TARGET, "") if touches else (PRIOR_ELSEWHERE, "never touched the agent's folder")
        if graph and touches:
            from .graph import alibi as graph_alibi  # imported here because graph.py uses git() from this module

            prior, reason = graph_alibi(repo, sha, target)
            alibi = reason if prior < 1.0 else ""
        suspects.append(Suspect(
            sha=sha, subject=subject, files=files, checkpoint=trailer.split()[0] if trailer.strip() else None,
            touches_target=touches, prior=prior, alibi=alibi,
        ))
    return suspects

    """A value inside the printed result, by a dotted path such as "output.tool_calls"."""
    for key in path.split("."):
        if not isinstance(result, dict) or key not in result:
            return None
        result = result[key]
    return result


def _fits(got, want) -> bool:
    """Whether an argument has the wanted value.

    A plain value has to be equal, with numbers compared to half a cent and strings without
    their outer spaces. A table asks for something looser and holds exactly one of: `in` (any
    of these), `contains` and `regex` (both ignoring case), `gte` and `lte`.
    """
    if isinstance(want, dict):
        if len(want) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"an argument matcher holds one of in, contains, regex, gte, lte, and this one holds {sorted(want)}")
        (how, value), = want.items()
        if how == "in":
            return any(_fits(got, one) for one in value)
        if how == "contains":
            return got is not None and str(value).lower() in str(got).lower()
        if how == "regex":
            return got is not None and re.search(value, str(got), re.IGNORECASE) is not None
        if how in ("gte", "lte"):
            number = isinstance(got, (int, float)) and not isinstance(got, bool)
            return number and (got >= value if how == "gte" else got <= value)
        raise ValueError(f"argument matcher {how!r} is not one of in, contains, regex, gte, lte")
    if isinstance(want, (int, float)) and not isinstance(want, bool):
        return isinstance(got, (int, float)) and not isinstance(got, bool) and math.isclose(got, want, abs_tol=0.005)
    if isinstance(want, str) and isinstance(got, str):
        return got.strip() == want.strip()
    return got == want


# What an input of a "calls" case may expect. Anything else in the input is a mistake and is refused,
# so a misspelt expectation cannot pass by being ignored.
CALLS_EXPECT = ("must_call", "must_not_call", "first_call", "call_counts", "call_sequence", "call_args",
                "reply_contains", "reply_not_contains", "reply_regex", "reply_not_regex")


def _calls_verdict(check: dict, expect: dict, result: dict) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Judge a run by the tools it called and what it said, read from the JSON it printed."""
    unknown = sorted(set(expect) - set(CALLS_EXPECT))
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"a calls check does not know {unknown}. It knows {', '.join(CALLS_EXPECT)}.")
    name_key, args_key = check.get("name", "name"), check.get("args", "args")
    calls = _at(result, check.get("calls", "tool_calls"))
    calls = [c for c in calls if isinstance(c, dict)] if isinstance(calls, list) else []
    names = [str(c.get(name_key)) for c in calls]
    reply = _at(result, check.get("reply", "reply"))
    reply = reply if isinstance(reply, str) else ""
    said = f"called {', '.join(names) or 'nothing'}"

    missing = [tool for tool in expect.get("must_call", []) if tool not in names]
    if missing:
        return False, f"never called {', '.join(missing)} ({said})"
    made = [tool for tool in expect.get("must_not_call", []) if tool in names]
    if made:
        return False, f"called {', '.join(made)}, which it should not have"
    first = expect.get("first_call")
    if first and names[:1] != [first]:
        return False, f"the first call was {names[0] if names else 'none'}, expected {first}"
    for tool, times in (expect.get("call_counts") or {}).items():
        if names.count(tool) != times:
            return False, f"called {tool} {names.count(tool)} times, expected {times}"
    rest = iter(names)
    if not all(any(name == tool for name in rest) for tool in expect.get("call_sequence", [])):
        return False, f"the calls were not in the order {', '.join(expect['call_sequence'])} ({said})"
    for wanted in expect.get("call_args", []):
        tool, args = wanted["tool"], wanted.get("args", {})
        tried = [c.get(args_key) if isinstance(c.get(args_key), dict) else {} for c in calls if c.get(name_key) == tool]
        if not any(all(_fits(given.get(key), value) for key, value in args.items()) for given in tried):
            return False, f"no call to {tool} had {json.dumps(args)}. It was called with {json.dumps(tried)}"
    low = reply.lower()
    absent = [text for text in expect.get("reply_contains", []) if text.lower() not in low]
    if absent:
        return False, f"the reply does not say {json.dumps(absent)}"
    present = [text for text in expect.get("reply_not_contains", []) if text.lower() in low]
    if present:
        return False, f"the reply says {json.dumps(present)}, which it should not"
    unmatched = [pattern for pattern in expect.get("reply_regex", []) if not re.search(pattern, reply, re.IGNORECASE)]
    if unmatched:
        return False, f"the reply does not match {json.dumps(unmatched)}"
    matched = [pattern for pattern in expect.get("reply_not_regex", []) if re.search(pattern, reply, re.IGNORECASE)]
    if matched:
        return False, f"the reply matches {json.dumps(matched)}, which it should not"
    return True, f"{said}, and the reply holds what it should"


def judge(case: Case, case_input: CaseInput, stdout: str, cwd: Path) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Return (passed, reason) for one run of the agent."""
    kind = case.check.get("kind", "refunds")
    result = last_json_line(stdout)
    if kind == "refunds":
        if result is None:
            return False, "the agent printed no JSON result"
        want = case_input.expect.get("refunds", [])
        got = result.get("refunds", [])
        if _same_refunds(got, want):
            return True, f"refunds match: {json.dumps(got)}"
        return False, f"refunds were {json.dumps(got)}, expected {json.dumps(want)}"
    if kind == "calls":
        # For any agent that prints its tool calls and its reply as JSON. The case says where in that
        # JSON they are (calls, name, args, reply), and each input says what a right run looks like.
        result = printed_json(stdout)
        if result is None:
            return False, "the agent printed no JSON result"
        return _calls_verdict(case.check, case_input.expect, result)
    if kind == "command":
        # The command gets the agent's stdout on stdin and the expectation in WHODUNIT_EXPECT. Exit 0 is a pass.
        done = subprocess.run(
            case.check["command"], input=stdout, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd, timeout=case.timeout,
            env={**os.environ, "WHODUNIT_EXPECT": json.dumps(case_input.expect)},
        )
        reason = (done.stdout.strip() or done.stderr.strip()).splitlines()[-1:] or [f"exit {done.returncode}"]
        return done.returncode == 0, reason[0]
    raise ValueError(f"check kind {kind!r} is not one of refunds, calls, command")

# Real re-run summary (signature bisect, weighted bisect, single repeat, throttling)

Target support-agent-demo, good `1b40b27` (verified: 18/19 executed cases pass at it; es2 fails there too, ca/ms skipped because
cancel_order does not exist yet), bad `f7d82b7` (HEAD before the tracing/flaky commits; all three regressions present). DEMO_FLAKE=0,
AGENT_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5, JUDGE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5 via the llm-proxy (concurrency 4, subscription backend), 1 repeat,
bad trace e2dad535... (rw1). Token baseline: merged calibration from 1b40b27 (3 repeats) plus ec19917 for the cancel_order cases
(`rerun2-baseline.json`). Without a baseline the harness skips token budgets, and R1/R2 are invisible (they only show as budget failures).

## Result per signature (run 2, after the fixes below)
| signature | culprit found | verdict | revert test |
|---|---|---|---|
| call_args:issue_refund.amount (R3, rw) | `b0be626` cents | CORRECT, confidence medium (revert conflicts flag) | passed 0% -> 100% |
| budget:tokens@refund_within_policy (rw) | `59c8b10` | plausible R2 (verify-with-search_help), confounded | failed 50% -> 50% |
| budget:tokens@order_status (os, R1 cases) | `59c8b10` | not a separate R1 culprit; same commit as above | failed 50% -> 0% |
| budget:tokens@policy_question (po, R2 cases) | `f7d82b7` | WRONG (borderline noise at the last commit) | failed 0% -> 50% |
| budget:tokens@escalation (es, R2 cases) | `ca150c7` | WRONG/unconfirmed | failed |
| budget:tokens@cancel_request (ca) | `96de44a` | unverified (revert inconclusive) | inconclusive |
| budget:tokens@multi_step (ms, R1 cases) | `22f7fbd` | unverified, 1 case, 1 sample | failed |
| call_args:escalate_to_human.priority (es2) | none | correctly refused: es2 fails at the good end too (not a regression) | n/a |

Success criteria: only R3 got its own culprit with a passing revert test. R1 and R2 were NOT separated: ground_truth.json only maps
cases to regressions (os/ms -> R1, po/es -> R2), not culprit commits, so the table scores case mapping and commit-message plausibility.
Every token regression inflates every category (the added tool schema and the search_help rule both lengthen every call), so
per-category budget signatures still mix R1 and R2 and the single-repeat token check is noisy near the 1.5x limit.

## Rounds
Primary (R3) investigation: 43 eval rounds including discovery. `compare` (separate empty caches): R3 plain 24 vs smart 21 rounds
(8 vs 7 steps), order_status budget plain 27 vs smart 24; same culprit both times. Smart wins by 3 rounds in both, but the
planner context was 21.7k tokens with the graph vs 43.3k reading the raw range (and 22.3k vs 39.4k). All 8 investigations: about 125
eval rounds plus compare reruns. Proxy totals for the whole session: 1417 calls (553 real CLI calls, 864 cache hits), 0 rate-limit
events, 0 backoff/recovered/gave_up events, 0 retries. No rate limiting was provoked at concurrency 4, so the live backoff path is
still only fake-tested.

## Bugs found and fixed (one commit each, 146 tests pass)
1. Budget regressions in different features collapsed into one `budget:tokens` signature; the suite only covered the bad trace's
   category (so R1/R2 cases never ran); one flaky rw3 run spawned three noise sibling investigations (call_args/must_call/call_counts).
   Fix: budget keys are `budget:tokens@<category>` (bare key still matches), `--all-categories`, signatures seen in a single run are
   re-run once and dropped if not reproduced (`signatures_unconfirmed`). Reviewer pass found three issues, all fixed.
2. A signature whose cases do not exist at the good end (cancel_order cases) made the good end "unusable". Now vacuously good.
   Resumed the two affected siblings; the other six ran on the code before this fix.
Run 1 (before fixes, `evidence/rerun1-prefix/`): R3 found at `b0be626`, budget at `59c8b10`, three noise siblings.

## Not verified / caveats
- Span divergence (neatlogs multi-span traces dead-letter, see neatlogs-dlq-report.md); intake picked good=d9b1680 from traces, overridden with --good.
- One sample per case per commit: budget verdicts near the limit flip, which is why po/es/ms culprits are unreliable. Raising `AGENTBISECT_REPEATS` was not tried.
- Haiku non-determinism (temperature cannot be set via the claude CLI); weighted-bisect optimality is not shown by 3-round differences.
- es2 and several cases are flaky/failing independent of the regressions.

- Budget signatures remain unreliable: every token regression (R1 tool schema, R2 search_help rule) inflates every category, so a

def stamp(record: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """What the status badge says, and whether it is the filled one. Only a case with a kept fix is closed."""
    lineup = record.get("lineup") or {}
    if lineup.get("clear"):
        return "No commit did it", ""
    if not lineup.get("culprit"):
        return "Open", ""
    if kept(record.get("fix")):
        return "Case closed", "closed"

This is one run on a repo that was not: [support-agent-demo](https://github.com/jaxsonsprinkles/support-agent-demo) by Jaxson Sprinkles, a customer-support agent built by another neatHack team as the target for their own tool, [AgentBisect](https://github.com/jaxsonsprinkles/agentbisect). The agent, its 30 commits, the coding sessions behind them, the eval cases and the seeded regressions are all theirs. None of its code or data is copied here. Each case file under `cases/outside/` holds one customer message and the checks from one of their eval cases, and names which. ## How it was kept blind - The range was given: `1b40b27` (good) to `0ecffc0` (bad), 25 commits. - Their answer key is published in the AgentBisect repo. That repo, the target's README and its history before the good ref were not opened until the predictions were committed and pushed. - [predictions.json](predictions.json) went in with commit `d1bf1b0`, pushed at 5:19 PM IST. The key was cloned after that. Commit 15 is `b0be626`. One attempt in the first lineup hit the gateway's rate limit, was voided and was run again. The third case fails at both ends, 6 of 6 and 6 of 6, so the lineup named nobody and said no commit in the range did it. The motive step worked on their repo, which I had not expected. Their checkpoint branch is published, so the request behind `b0be626` came out of its Entire checkpoint, was found word for word in the session transcript, and `entire why` put all 12 changed lines that were checked behind that commit and checkpoint. The request asked for refund amounts in cents "to match Stripe", with the change kept to the refund tool and its tests. ## What the key says [ground_truth.json](https://github.com/jaxsonsprinkles/agentbisect/blob/main/evidence/ground_truth.json) maps each of their 24 eval cases to one of three seeded regressions, R1, R2 and R3, or to "control". It names no commits. Their notes beside it (`evidence/rerun-summary.md` and `evidence/rerun3-summary.md`) say what the three are: R3 is the refund amount in cents, at `b0be626`. R1 and R2 are changes that make every run use more tokens, one through a tool schema and one through a rule about `search_help`, and their notes point at `59c8b10` for R2 and name no commit for R1. They also say R1 and R2 "only show as budget failures", meaning a run is counted as broken when it uses more than one and a half times the tokens it used at the good ref. Scored against that: - refund-amount: right. The key puts rw1 under R3, and Whodunit named R3's commit. - escalation-skipped: not backed by the key. The key puts es2 under R2, the token regression, and Whodunit named R3's commit. What the replays show is a different symptom from the one the key means. Before `b0be626` the agent sent an 800.00 refund request to a person every time, and from that commit on it issued the refund itself every time. That commit reworded the tool's own rule that refunds over $500 must be escalated. So this may be a side effect of R3 that the key does not list, or it may be something only the model on this gateway does. Nobody has reverted the commit to find out, and I am not counting it as a hit. - out-of-window: agrees with the key. ro1 is a control, and Whodunit named nobody. - R1 and R2: not found, and not looked for. Every request their key files under R1 or R2 still called the right tools and said the right things at the bad ref, twice each, except es1, which fails the same way at both ends. A check on tools and replies cannot see a run that is right and costs more. The token counts were there to see: the same order-status request used 4,562 input tokens at the bad ref and a refund request that used 2,904 at the good ref used 4,576 at the bad one. No case was opened on them, because the cases were to come from the repo's own checks. So, plainly: of three seeded regressions, Whodunit named the commit behind one. It made two accusations, one confirmed by the key and one the key does not back. It called one range clear, correctly. Their notes also record a behaviour at the tip commit, cancelling an unshipped order when the customer only asked where it was, which their tool caught. All five of their order-status requests passed 2 times in 2 here at the tip, so no case was opened for it. ## What it cost All of it ran on the hackathon gateway's small model, two replays at a time, with token counts taken from what the agent prints and priced at $1 and $5 per million. - Screening their 24 eval inputs at the bad ref twice, and the ones that failed at the good ref twice: 67 runs, 359,913 input tokens and 13,379 output tokens, about $0.43. - The three lineups: 56 replays, about $0.41. - About $0.83 in all, against a cap of $2.50 the owner set. ## What had to change in Whodunit - A check that is not about refunds. `kind = "calls"` reads the JSON an agent prints and checks which tools it called, which it did not, the first call, counts, order, arguments, and what the reply says or matches. The case says where in the JSON the calls and the reply are. An expectation it does not know is refused, so a misspelt one cannot pass by being ignored. - Reading a result that is pretty-printed over many lines. The refund agent prints one line. - Handing an agent its key under the agent's own name. `[env_from]` in a case maps the agent's variable to the name of one in the runner's `.env`. Only names are written down. - A longer wait after a provider error, set per case, because this gateway limits by the minute and the first screening run lost 15 attempts to that at three at a time. - Token counts on each replay, when the agent reports them. - A record keeps the address of the repo it was run on, so the page links the culprit's own Entire page. No file in their repo was edited. The gateway was reached through environment variables alone. ## What did not carry over - Alibis. The agent sits at the root of its repo, so the path filter excuses nobody, and entire-graph was not set up in the clone. All 25 commits started equal. A README-only commit was as suspect as the rest. - Traces. The agent's own tracing was switched off for these replays so that its runs went to nobody's neatlogs project. So there is no failing run set against a passing one, and no brief. - Damages. Those are still read from the refund agent's tool spans. - The fix. It was not run, on purpose. Their repo is theirs to fix. - The model. Their notes say they ran the agent on its pinned model through their own proxy. These replays used the gateway's small model, which may not be the same version. Two of their cases that they report passing at the good ref fail there here, and their es2 fails at the good ref in both places. ## What was not checked - Whether the skipped escalation really starts at `b0be626` on their pinned model. That needs their setup, or a revert, and neither was done. - Whether a token check would have found R1 and R2. It was not built. - The lineups were run once each. At temperature 0 the agent is close to deterministic, which is why 22 replays were enough, and why these two cases say little about the statistical part of the bisect. 4. questions the planner or a coding agent wrote (kept in the database until you save them).

## Rules

Code, no model, every span.

```yaml
id: repeated-tool-call
kind: rule
title: Same tool called repeatedly with identical arguments
rule:
  type: repeat            # repeat | errors | count | threshold | match | run_end
  span: { type: [tool, mcp_tool] }
  same: [tool, input]
  at_least: 3
guidance: >-
  You have called {tool} {count} times with the same arguments ({args}) ...
action: flag              # or halt (your own rules only)
```

| type | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `repeat` | `at_least` matching spans share the `same` fields; resolves when the next call differs |
| `errors` | `consecutive` matching spans failed in a row |
| `count` | the run has `at_least` matching spans |
| `threshold` | a run metric (`total_tokens`, `llm_calls`, `duration_ms`, …) reaches `at_least` |
| `match` | a regex matches a span's `input`, `output`, `error` or `name` |
| `run_end` | the run ended with `error`, `no_output` or `interrupted` |

## Questions

Answered by the decision model with a probability. Yes/no questions are phrased as failures, so a
high probability always means a problem.

```yaml
id: refund-without-ownership
kind: yes_no              # yes_no | choice | score
scope: trace              # span | trace | session
ask: Did the agent issue a refund without first confirming the customer owns the order?
evidence:
  spans: { type: tool, name: [lookup_order, issue_refund] }
  fields: [input, output, status]
  last: 12
  final_output: false
when: live                # live (as spans arrive, and at run end) | end
flag_at: 0.8
guidance: Confirm the customer owns the order before issuing a refund.
applies_to: { workflow: refund-agent }
```

`choice` questions take `options` (label → description) and `flag_on`; `score` questions take
`levels` and `flag_at_level`.

### Make sure a question can see what it asks about

- `scope: span` judges one call at a time: right for "Did this tool call pass a negative amount?".
- `scope: trace` sees the run's spans in order: right whenever a question relates two things, such
  as a tool's result and what the agent said next.
- A question about the agent's answer ("claims", "says", "reports", "the final response") needs
  `scope: trace` and `evidence.final_output: true`. `neatroots checks validate`, the app's check
  editor and the MCP check tools warn when a check asks about the answer but can't see it; a check
  drafted from a plain-language concern is given that evidence automatically.
- Preview a new check on at least one run that has the problem and one that doesn't.

"""Count the recorded refund-agent runs that issued a refund with no lookup before it, by where their commit sits.

This is the headline case turned into something to watch for: `issue_refund` called in a run where no
`lookup_order` came first. It reads neatroots, uses no model, and prints one JSON object.

    uv run python eval/standing_check.py
"""

import json
import subprocess
from collections import Counter

from whodunit.neat import neatroots, select_all

CULPRIT = "ced2ecd21c3ed165a1a729e17f68d2000cdc19ca"  # cases/whole-history.record.json, lineup.culprit
FIX = "7e8120e7a5bd05c5d54b542b8a2794fdbd6fc229"  # the same record, fix.commit


def holds(ancestor: str, sha: str) -> bool:
    return subprocess.run(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", ancestor, sha], capture_output=True).returncode == 0


def main() -> None:
    mcp = neatroots()
    runs = select_all(mcp, "select r.trace_id, s.attributes from runs r join spans s on s.trace_id = r.trace_id and s.name = 'run_info' "
                           "where r.workflow = 'refund-agent' and r.complete = 1", cap=20000)
    flagged = {row["trace_id"] for row in select_all(
        mcp, "select distinct f.trace_id from spans f where f.name = 'issue_refund' and not exists "
             "(select 1 from spans l where l.trace_id = f.trace_id and l.name = 'lookup_order' and l.start_ms < f.start_ms)", cap=20000)}
    where: dict[str, str] = {}
    seen, hits = Counter(), Counter()
    for row in runs:
        tags = json.loads(row["attributes"]).get("neatlogs.tags") or json.loads(row["attributes"]).get("tags") or row["attributes"]
        text = tags if isinstance(tags, str) else json.dumps(tags)
        at = text.find("commit:")
        sha = "".join(ch for ch in text[at + 7:at + 47] if ch in "0123456789abcdef") if at >= 0 else ""
        if len(sha) < 7:
            place = "no commit tag"
        else:
            if sha not in where:
                known = subprocess.run(["git", "cat-file", "-e", f"{sha}^{{commit}}"], capture_output=True).returncode == 0
                where[sha] = ("commit not in this repo" if not known else "at the kept fix" if holds(FIX, sha)
                              else "from the culprit on, unfixed" if holds(CULPRIT, sha) else "before the culprit")
            place = where[sha]
        seen[place] += 1
        hits[place] += row["trace_id"] in flagged
    print(json.dumps({"runs": sum(seen.values()), "flagged": sum(hits.values()),
                      "by_place": {place: {"runs": seen[place], "flagged": hits[place]} for place in sorted(seen)}}, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

# Business plan inputs

These are the numbers and assumptions to build the cfo.ai model from. The measured ones come from this repo's runs on 10 and 11 October 2026. The assumed ones are marked and are the owner's to change.

One thing to keep in view when quoting any of it: no real customer has used the refund agent. Its ordinary traffic was sent by `eval/traffic.py`, a script that plays customers against each commit, and the shop and its orders are test data. The replay costs below are real spend on real model calls. The refund amounts are what a script's requests cost a test shop.

## What is being sold

Whodunit Cloud: hosted investigations for teams that run an AI agent in production. The command line tool stays open source and free with your own keys. The paid product is the hosted replay workers, the case file pages, the regression checks in CI, and the standing rulings shared across a team.

## Unit costs, measured

Six full investigations on the refund agent, with replays on a small hosted model at list price:

| Case | Replays | Replay cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| cents-off | 89 | $0.34 |
| strangers-paid | 112 | $0.39 |
| whole-history | 176 | $0.80 |
| turned-away | 171 | $0.95 |
| wrong-order-refunded | 274 | $1.00 |
| half-done-batch | 558 | $3.53 |

- Median replay cost per investigation: about $0.87. Mean: about $1.17. The worst case is a rare bug that was never fixed. These are higher than the first version of this table, because every kept fix is now also replayed against 12 or 13 other requests, and the headline case needed a second patch.
- Brief and patch calls on a larger model: about $0.10 to $0.30 per investigation.
- Replay worker: one t3.large at about $61 a month runs three replays at a time. Assumed: one worker per 15 paying teams.
- So the cost of one investigation is about $1.37 on average for an agent on a small model. An agent on a large model costs roughly 5 to 15 times more to replay, which is why replays are billed at cost above the included amount.

The requests were sent by `eval/traffic.py`, not by customers, so these show the size of the thing and are not a measurement of any real shop. Each line counts only the runs that failed that case's own check:

- One prompt change refunded 120.00 to the wrong people, in 4 of the 6 scripted requests that asked for it.
- One "friendlier replies" change withheld 360.00, across all 6 scripted requests that were owed a refund: three of 90.00 and three of 30.00.

| Extra investigations | $8 each | |
| Replays on the customer's larger model | at cost plus 20% | |

Gross margin on Team at full use: 40 investigations at $1.37 is $55, plus about $4 of worker share, against $249. About 76%.

import json

PLAN = Path("pitch/plan.json")
REACHED = "the spend limit was reached"


def read_plan(path: str | Path = PLAN) -> dict | None:
    path = Path(path)
    return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.is_file() else None


def spend_limit(plan: dict) -> float:
    """The most one investigation may spend, in dollars, if the plan's margin on a Team agent is to hold.

        limit = (team price x (1 - target margin) - worker cost / agents per worker) / investigations included

    A Team agent pays the price each month. Keeping the margin leaves price x (1 - margin) for
    serving it. Its share of a replay worker comes off that, and the rest is spread over the
    investigations the tier includes, as if all of them were used. An investigation that stays
    under this cannot be the one that breaks the margin.
    """
    serving = plan["team_price_usd"] * (1 - plan["target_margin"])
    worker = plan["worker_monthly_cost_usd"] / plan["team_agents_per_shared_worker"]
    return round((serving - worker) / plan["team_investigations_included"], 2)


@dataclass
class Meter:
    """Adds up what one investigation has spent and says when that reaches its limit.

    Replays are priced the way the damages are: token counts from the runs' model spans in
    neatroots, at list prices. The model calls for the brief and the patch are not metered, so
    the plan's allowance for them is counted as spent from the start. A replay still being
    written to neatroots is not counted yet, so the meter runs a few replays behind.
    """

    limit: float
    case_id: str
    source: str = str(PLAN)  # where the limit came from: the plan file, or the flag
    raised: bool = False  # whether the flag set it above what the plan allows
    allowance: float = 0.0
    windows: list = field(default_factory=list)  # earlier stretches of this investigation's replays, in ms
    ask: Callable[[], Mcp] = neatroots
    started_ms: float = field(default_factory=lambda: time.time() * 1000 - 2000)
    unknown: str = ""  # why the replays could not be priced, if neatroots could not be asked
    stopped: str = ""  # the step that was stopped, once one has been

    def spent(self) -> float:
        stretches = [*self.windows, [self.started_ms, time.time() * 1000 + 60000]]
        mine = REPLAY.format(like=f"%case:{self.case_id}%".replace("'", "''"))
        mine += " and (" + " or ".join(f"(r.started_ms >= {float(lo)} and r.started_ms <= {float(hi)})" for lo, hi in stretches) + ")"
        try:
            return self.allowance + _spend(self.ask(), mine, PRICES)[0]
        except NeatError as exc:
            self.unknown = str(exc)
            return self.allowance

    def why(self) -> str:
        """Why the investigation has to stop here, or nothing if it may go on."""
        spent = self.spent()
        return f"{REACHED}: about ${spent:.2f} spent of ${self.limit:.2f} allowed" if spent >= self.limit else ""

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        said = {"limit_usd": self.limit, "from": self.source, "raised": self.raised, "spent_usd": round(self.spent(), 4),
                "allowance_usd": self.allowance, "stopped": self.stopped}
        if self.unknown:
            said["note"] = f"neatroots could not be asked what the replays cost, so only the allowance was counted: {self.unknown}"
        return said

"""The business plan sets a spend limit, and an investigation that reaches it stops and says so."""

import json

import pytest

from tests.planted import stub_history
from tests.test_lineup import flaky
from whodunit import casefile
from whodunit.cli import load_record, main
from whodunit.lineup import statistical_bisect
from whodunit.neat import NeatError
from whodunit.plan import REACHED, Meter, meter_for, read_plan, spend_limit

PLAN = {"team_price_usd": 249, "team_investigations_included": 40, "target_margin": 0.7639, "worker_monthly_cost_usd": 61,
        "team_agents_per_shared_worker": 15, "brief_and_patch_cost_per_investigation_usd": 0.2}


class Spent:
    """Stands in for neatroots: every question about replays gets these token counts back."""

    def __init__(self, prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int = 0):
        self.rows = [{"model": "claude-haiku", "pt": prompt_tokens, "ct": completion_tokens}]

    def call(self, tool, **arguments):
        return {"rows": self.rows}


def test_the_limit_is_read_from_the_plan_file(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "plan.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(PLAN))
    # (249 x (1 - 0.7639) - 61 / 15) / 40
    assert spend_limit(read_plan(path)) == pytest.approx(1.37)
    assert spend_limit({**PLAN, "target_margin": 0.5}) == pytest.approx(3.01)
    meter = meter_for("c", {"replay_windows": [[1, 2]]}, path=path)
    assert meter.limit == pytest.approx(1.37) and meter.allowance == 0.2 and meter.source == str(path) and not meter.raised and meter.windows == [[1, 2]]
    raised = meter_for("c", {}, given=5.0, path=path)
    assert raised.limit == 5.0 and raised.raised and raised.source == "--spend-limit"
    assert not meter_for("c", {}, given=1.0, path=path).raised  # lowering it is not raising it
    assert meter_for("c", {}, path=tmp_path / "none.json") is None and read_plan(tmp_path / "none.json") is None


def test_the_plan_in_the_repo_gives_the_limit_the_readme_quotes():
    plan = read_plan()
    assert plan["team_price_usd"] == 249 and plan["team_investigations_included"] == 40
    assert spend_limit(plan) == pytest.approx(1.37)


def test_the_meter_prices_replays_like_the_damages_and_counts_the_allowance():
    under = Meter(limit=1.37, case_id="c", allowance=0.2, ask=lambda: Spent(1_000_000))  # $1.00 of replays
    assert under.spent() == pytest.approx(1.20) and under.why() == ""
    over = Meter(limit=1.37, case_id="c", allowance=0.2, ask=lambda: Spent(1_000_000, 40_000))  # $1.20 of replays
    assert over.why() == f"{REACHED}: about $1.40 spent of $1.37 allowed"

    def down():
        raise NeatError("connection refused")
    blind = Meter(limit=1.37, case_id="c", allowance=0.2, ask=down)
    assert blind.why() == "" and "connection refused" in blind.to_dict()["note"]


def test_a_lineup_that_would_cross_the_limit_stops_and_names_nobody():
    asked = []

    def stop() -> str:
        asked.append(1)
        return f"{REACHED}: about $1.40 spent of $1.37 allowed" if len(asked) > 2 else ""
    found = statistical_bisect(40, flaky(25, 0.3, seed=3), budget=400, stop=stop)
    assert found.culprit is None and found.note.startswith(REACHED)
    assert found.replays < 40 and len(found.remaining) > 1  # handed back with the suspects still in play
    free = statistical_bisect(40, flaky(25, 0.3, seed=3), budget=400)
    assert free.culprit == 25 and free.replays > found.replays


def test_the_record_says_why_a_lineup_stopped_and_when_the_limit_was_raised(tmp_path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    def down():
        raise NeatError("not running")
    monkeypatch.setattr("whodunit.plan.neatroots", down)
    made = stub_history(tmp_path / "repo", suspects=12, culprit=5, broken=(3,))
    assert main(["lineup", str(made["case"]), "--repo", str(made["repo"]), "--budget", "60", "--spend-limit", "0"]) == 1
    assert "Stopped: the spend limit was reached" in capsys.readouterr().out
    record = load_record(made["case"].with_suffix(".record.json"))
    assert record["lineup"]["culprit"] is None and record["lineup"]["note"].startswith(REACHED)
    assert len(record["lineup"]["remaining"]) > 1 and all("probability" in s for s in record["lineup"]["remaining"])
    assert record["spend"]["stopped"] == "lineup" and record["spend"]["limit_usd"] == 0 and record["spend"]["from"] == "--spend-limit"
    assert ("spend", "Stopped during the lineup at the spend limit: about $0.00 spent of $0.00 allowed, a limit set by --spend-limit.") in casefile.timeline(record)
    # With room to spend, the same case names its culprit and the record says nothing stopped it.
    assert main(["lineup", str(made["case"]), "--repo", str(made["repo"]), "--budget", "60", "--spend-limit", "50"]) == 0
    record = load_record(made["case"].with_suffix(".record.json"))
    assert record["lineup"]["culprit"]["sha"] == made["culprit"] and record["spend"]["stopped"] == ""

# The demo video

`whodunit-demo.mp4` is 2 minutes 16 seconds, 1920 by 1080, with a narrator, captions and a synthesized score. It runs thirteen scenes: the question, one failing run, a title card, the command, the lineup, the motive, the fix, before and after, the trace and the damage, the sealed eval, the plan, the

The narration is a synthesized voice, made with ElevenLabs from the script in `build_film.py`. Each scene is as long as its narration clip, and the events in a scene fire where the words fall.

An earlier cut, 89 seconds with captions and no voice, is kept beside it as `whodunit-v1-captions-only.mp4`.

What is here is the part of the film that is ours:

- `film.json`: the thirteen scenes, their timing in beats, the captions and the camera moves.
- `build_film.py`: the narration script, and the code that times every scene to its clip.
- `screens.tsx`: Whodunit's screens rebuilt so each row and mark can move: the git log, one failing run, the command, the lineup, the Entire checkpoint, the two exhibits, the two fix attempts, before and after, the neatlogs trace, the damages, the docket cards, the cash chart and the three tools.
- `data.json`: the 57 suspects, the ordinary runs and the four replay rounds of the headline case, copied from its record.
- `contact-sheet.png`: sixteen stills from the last third of the film.

The motion template the film runs on is not in the repo, because it is not ours to publish.

## What is real and what is drawn

Every number is from a case record, the cfo.ai model or the neatlogs dashboard. The request and the reply in the chat scene are word for word from the failing run. The lineup plays the record's own four rounds.

The screens are redrawn, so they are not screenshots. The exhibit steps are shortened. The trace shows 13 of the run's 17 steps. The cash chart is drawn from the model's monthly figures and is not cfo.ai's own chart.
